items.title: HRV ↔ RHR coupling
items.why: When you are actually recovering, HRV rises as resting HR falls — same autonomic story, two sensors. A solid negative r is an integrity check Garmin never puts on one chart. If the link goes slack while one number looks 'fine', believe the decoupling: residual stress or poor sleep architecture, not a PR. Lever: protect the night after Capoeira before chasing more intensity.

items.title: Hours still drive score?
items.why: If hours and score still move together, bedtime length is the lever — not another sleep gadget. A weak r means stages or timing are stealing the score (late Capoeira, split nights with a one-year-old). You already run a chronic ~2h debt vs Garmin need; stretching time-in-bed after hard evenings beats optimizing deep %.

items.title: Capoeira → next sleep
items.teaser: Nights after evening hard run 37 min shorter
items.why: Across this window, sleep after Capoeira/evening-hard is 37 min shorter than other nights. Late intensity delays cooldown into bedtime — that is a timing tax, not proof you 'can't handle' the class. Book 8h+ in bed on those nights and keep the cool-down walk; do not stack a hard morning 3k unless HRV/RHR stayed green.

items.title: Intensity → next debt
items.teaser: r = 0.17 · hard minutes vs next-night debt
items.why: Vigorous + moderate minutes today predicting more sleep debt tomorrow means the session is winning the calendar. At 37, with kids and a recomp goal, that is the wrong trade: you cannot out-train a standing 2h nightly hole. If r stays useful (~0.3+), treat a hard day as a sleep appointment, not a suggestion.

items.title: Stress → next HRV
items.teaser: r = -0.24 · life load leaving a next-morning mark
items.why: A negative lag means today's sympathetic load is still in tomorrow's HRV — life stress, not just training fatigue. That separates 'I trained hard' from 'the day never came down'. When this lights up, the move is an easier morning and earlier lights-out, not another quality session.

items.title: Steps on short-sleep days
items.why: If you walk more on the nights you already under-slept, you are not auto-deloading — you are stacking life load on a deficit. That pattern is common with kids + stroller mornings and it quietly blocks fat-loss. A green here would be fewer steps or true easy movement after a short night.

items.title: Fitness–recovery gap
items.why: Engine up, overnight recharge not paying down: classic 'fit but under-recovered' split after miluim and with young kids. Leaner/defined needs the debt to fall, not just a prettier RHR. If this is amber/red, steal sleep from evening intensity before adding more quality work.

items.title: Run → walk HR recovery
items.why: The walk is the test, not bonus cardio. Min HR on that 8–15 min stroll is the recovery number; stroller 3ks cost more than free pace shows, so they stay annotated and are not mixed into solo grades. Target longer easy cool-downs (10–15 min) and a falling min HR — that is the habit, not another interval.
